sampling_model.design: Deterministic quasi-uniform triangular arrays in a fixed bounded Lipschitz domain in \(d\in\{1,2\}\), with \(h_N\asymp N^{-1/d}\) and separation comparable to \(h_N\).
sampling_model.units: The observed units are sites \(s_{i,N}\); uncertainty comes from one centered stationary bivariate Gaussian-field realization evaluated at those sites.
sampling_model.treatment: The continuous exposure is \(X(s_{i,N})\), and the homogeneous conditional slope in \(Y(s)=\beta X(s)+W(s)\) is the target.
sampling_model.overlap: No exposure nugget or nonspatial variation is assumed; identification comes from the smoother signed cross-tail with \(p\in[p_{\min},p_{\max}]\subset(1/2,1)\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Only the marginal microergodic scale ratio \(\gamma=c_W/c_X\) is estimated by residual quadratic variations; \(p\), \(A\), and the nonmicroergodic ranges are profiled or bounded over their stipulated compact sets.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: High-frequency dissipation of exposure--confounder coherence supplies sufficient identification and motivates spectral adjustment.
Relative local smoothness conditions characterize consistent slope estimability and local differences or Laplacians yield consistent estimators.
Locally preconditioned inversion-free covariance estimators are root-\(N\) consistent and asymptotically normal on multidimensional irregular lattices.
Higher-order quadratic variations consistently estimate Mat\'ern smoothness and microergodic parameters on three structured irregular-design families.
Appropriately filtered smoothed spatial cross-periodograms on lattices are relatively consistent and asymptotically normal.
The scalar Mat\'ern microergodic parameter has root-\(N\) Gaussian behavior uniformly over a compact nuisance range with known smoothness.
Conditional quasi-likelihood-ratio tests have uniformly correct asymptotic size without restrictions on identification strength.
A plurality-rule aggregate mode consistently estimates the spatial slope, and valid candidate slopes are asymptotically normal.

body.tldr: Three exact affine-annihilating local slopes generate a finite-dimensional mean cone \(\beta\mathbf 1+B_Nq_N(p)\) whose secants and tangents remain uniformly separated from the slope direction. The actual quasi-uniform-design Gaussian experiment and feasible scale studentization yield conservative uniform inference, root-\(N\) diameter and risk, and matching lower bounds through every vanishing signed cross-tail. In addition, the exact least-favorable Gaussian critical value over the physically attainable amplitude--exponent set is attained and gives asymptotic observed-law lower-envelope coverage equal to \(1-\alpha\), with a pathwise \(O(N^{-1/2})\) diameter through zero, local, divergent, endpoint, elbow, and nonconvergent-design regimes. This equality is not a finite-sample observed-law claim, and a terminating certified numerical approximation of the exact critical value remains open.

project_justification.gap: Published spatial-confounding results identify or consistently estimate slopes under local spectral separation, and published fixed-domain results deliver Gaussian inference for scalar covariance combinations. They do not provide actual-design, design-uniform slope inference or exact least-favorable asymptotic profile calibration when the observation-scale signed cross-tail is local to zero and its exponent is unidentified.
project_justification.niche: The exact Mat\'ern-one-half, no-nugget model isolates a nonregular finite-dimensional nuisance cone in which three scales separate \(\beta\) uniformly. Exact affine filters control arbitrary quasi-uniform designs in dimensions one and two, while the physical amplitude set distinguishes bounded, divergent, endpoint, and elbow regimes.
project_justification.fill: The project derives the actual-design Gaussian experiment, feasible residual-scale studentization, conservative uniform coverage, root-\(N\) diameter and risk, matching honest lower bounds, and an exact attained Gaussian critical value whose profile set has asymptotic observed-law lower-envelope coverage equal to \(1-\alpha\). Certified numerical evaluation of the continuum critical-value maximum is retained as a separate open question.

body.related_work: Guan, Page, Reich, Ventrucci and Yang motivate the problem by showing that decay of high-frequency exposure--confounder coherence can identify a spatial slope; their spectral construction informs the observation-scale tail parameter used here. Datta and Stein characterize consistent infill estimability and construct local-difference and Laplacian estimators over broad Gaussian-field classes; their result informs the local-filter architecture, while the present inference theorem is for the narrower no-nugget signed-cross-tail class. Keshavarz, Nguyen and Scott obtain root-\(N\) Gaussian covariance estimation from preconditioned quadratic forms on irregular lattices, and Loh, Sun and Wen develop higher-order variations on selected irregular designs; both inform the finite-matrix proof. Lim and Stein prove normality of filtered cross-periodograms on lattices and inform the cross-form covariance analysis. Zhang studies scalar Mat\'ern microergodic equivalence, while Li studies Bayesian posterior and Bernstein--von Mises behavior for Mat\'ern covariance parameters. Andrews and Mikusheva inform weak-identification calibration but do not analyze this spatial curved cone or its tangent and endpoint limits. Burman, Ogburn and Datta provide the conditional county-centroid PM2.5 and COVID-19 consumer and a distinct plurality-based identifying model. The exact critical value proved here is an attained mathematical Gaussian quantile; no cited work or present argument supplies its terminating certified continuum computation.
body.technical_internal_limitation: First differences are insufficient in \(d=2\): the analytic covariance remainder creates an \(O(h_N)\) slope bias and normalized correlations of order \(1/r\) create a logarithmic variance factor. Exact affine annihilation removes the quadratic covariance term and yields summable fourth-difference dependence. Three-scale profile intervals may nevertheless have large constants when \(p_{\min}\) is close to \(1/2\); the proposal claims rate optimality, not an efficient constant.
body.honest_scope: The model is restricted to deterministic quasi-uniform designs in dimensions one and two, no nugget, known marginal smoothness one-half, stationary Gaussian fields, compact scale and range nuisance, and the stated signed parametric cross-tail. The exact-attainable profile set has asymptotic observed-law lower-envelope coverage equal to \(1-\alpha\) and pathwise root-\(N\) diameter; only its Gaussian reference calibration is exact at fixed \(N\). A terminating certified numerical approximation of the exact continuum critical value is not proved, so the conservative chi-square critical value remains the directly specified fallback. The scope excludes unknown marginal-smoothness adaptation, nonstationarity, independent Fourier-coordinate approximations, and broader covariance classes. The county-centroid PM2.5 and COVID-19 use is conditional on empirical Mat\'ern and quasi-uniform-design diagnostics and does not itself establish a nonparametric causal estimand.
